gates.reason: Temporary filesystem writes use generated directories and fixed/joined test paths; traversal and uncapped-read protections are exercised.
Parser and resolver assertions use reproducible fixtures and verify truncation, ordering, deduplication, and byte-count behavior.
The tests explicitly cover artifact byte caps, tail-only JSONL reads, and directory-entry limits that bound ingest memory and work.
Filesystem mutations are confined to UUID-named temporary paths and cleaned up; no command execution, credentials, or untrusted path components are used.
Timing medians, percentages, corpus counts, and structured summary fields were re-derived; emitted walk counts consistently use the eight assembleArtifacts paths.
This is the performance probe itself, measuring parser, cold/warm assembly, artifact-cache, walk-count, and latency-share behavior over a deterministic corpus.
Initial and final redirect URLs are checked against the registered source allowlist, fetched content is converted to text, and no OAuth credentials or ~/.claude content are transmitted.

Snapshots retain per-page URL, fetch time, content hash, validators, extracted content, and registered facts; drift and stale output include reproducible hashes, changed URLs, and dated refresh evidence.
External response bodies are fully materialized without a byte budget, allowing excessive ingest memory and latency.
Tests cover both off-allowlist registry URLs and off-allowlist redirect targets, plus safe single-pass entity decoding.
Tests verify per-page provenance hashes, extracted fact values, independent fact-page drift, unchanged-page reuse, and dated staleness behavior.
This unit-test file is not a hot path and contains no performance surface or benchmark calculation.

findings.title: Guidance ingestion has no response-body size budget
findings.what: fetchPage calls response.text() and then creates additional derived strings and hashes without checking Content-Length or enforcing a streamed byte cap. An oversized response from an allowed external source can therefore consume unbounded memory and substantially delay or terminate the ingest job.
findings.fix: Read the response body through a size-limited stream with a documented maximum, reject an excessive Content-Length up front when present, and abort once streamed bytes exceed that same limit.
findings.acceptance: Add a fetch fixture whose body exceeds the configured limit, assert buildSnapshot rejects with a stable size-limit error without processing the full body, and retain a boundary test proving a body exactly at the limit succeeds.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that the only body acquisition at scripts/ingest-guidance.mjs:162 is an unrestricted response.text(); the surrounding allowlist, status, and redirect checks at lines 138-160 impose no response-size or processing budget.
